mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen 11.9 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w, indicating sustained recovery momentum. This trend will continue over the next four weeks as baseline behavioral patterns stabilize, driving RETAIL_REC higher than the preceding 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -37.3% to -25.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below the mean of the preceding 28 days, or declines week-on-week for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage has improved 6.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w. When TRANSIT rises above -65%, commuter confidence increases, enabling retail foot traffic to recover. This mechanism operates over a one-week lag.
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls back below -65% and RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week, or RETAIL_REC declines despite TRANSIT remaining above -65%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 18.1% to 14.0%, signaling reduced home confinement. Simultaneously, RETAIL_REC has risen 11.9 points. The joint signal of decreasing residential time and increasing retail activity indicates sustained behavioral shift toward out-of-home consumption over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while RETAIL_REC rises in same period
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 4.1 points while RETAIL_REC rose 11.9 points
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 16% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously declines, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has deteriorated from -37.9% to -31.6% (6.3 point improvement), but remains severely suppressed. If WORKPLACES fails to improve further over the next two weeks, retail recovery will stall as consumer spending power remains constrained by reduced employment activity.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improvement rate slows to less than 3 percentage points per week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES remains at -31.6%, still 32 points below baseline
failure_condition: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 percentage points in the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed from 7.3% to -28.3% over one week, a 35.6 point drop. This sharp reversal suggests weather or policy-driven outdoor activity constraints. When outdoor recreation is suppressed, consumers redirect discretionary time to indoor retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 20 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 7.3% to -28.3% in one week
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above 0% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not increase, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has shifted from negative to positive territory (t-0w: +2.1%), indicating essential-goods confidence. When essential-goods mobility turns positive, consumer confidence broadens to discretionary retail. This interaction between essential and discretionary spending drives RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to positive
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls back below 0% and RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the preceding 28-day mean, or RETAIL_REC declines despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining positive.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both severely suppressed (-60.7% and -31.6% respectively). If both remain below their current levels over the next two weeks, commuting infrastructure will not support retail recovery, and RETAIL_REC will decline or stagnate.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show zero or negative week-on-week change
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 percentage points in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined 4.1 points from t-3w to t-0w, indicating policy-driven or voluntary reduction in home time. This regime shift toward out-of-home activity will sustain RETAIL_REC recovery if RESIDENTIAL continues declining over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 18.1% to 14.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 17% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the preceding 28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to decline.
